messages:
maria_support: FYI — ticket from Acme (enterprise) reporting spikes of 5xx and timeouts to hosted /v1/generate this morning. They're seeing ~10% failures and a bunch of gateway timeouts. I have the original curl they used below.

maria_support: curl they ran (customer):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxxx' -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"hello","max_tokens":256}' -v
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (13.224.0.1) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> ...
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"gateway timeout"}
```

maria_support: Observed timestamps from customer: failures spike ~2024-03-08T14:22:xxZ, correlated to several 10s+ latencies. They attached our request-id: rqd:abcd-1234 (I've included it below).

aj_oncall: Pinging SRE/runtime. @sam_sre @jin_runtime — can you grab telemetry for that request-id and the last 30m of queue/backlog metrics?

sam_sre: On it. Pulling metrics now. Quick note: we had a minor deploy earlier but nothing that should change queue limits.

sam_sre: PromQL I'm running:
```
sum by (instance) (redwood_runtime_queue_length{env="prod"})
```

sam_sre: Initial look: around 14:22 UTC we have a sudden queue_depth climb from baseline ~50 to peaks ~1200 across the serving cluster. p95/p99 token latency also jumps (p99 ~12s). Gateway (nginx) times out at 10s which matches customer's timeouts.

jin_runtime: That pattern screams continuous-batching backlog + queue depth saturation. When the batching window and incoming burst combine, the queue holds many in-flight requests waiting for batch formation. If queue depth reaches queue_limit, runtime starts returning 502/504 early (we have a circuit that fails fast to avoid OOM).

maria_support: Customer says they had a big traffic blast after a marketing email — sounds like sudden spike.

dana_cs: Confirmed. They admitted a 5x traffic surge for a 10m window at ~14:20. They were using our hosted endpoint with default rate settings.

aj_oncall: Can we reproduce in staging so we have a concrete repro and mitigation test? If so, what's the minimal repro command?

jin_runtime: Yes. Repro steps (staging):
1) Deploy the same model variant with default runtime config (BATCH_WINDOW_MS=10, MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH=512)
2) Run a burst script to send N concurrent requests with small payloads and sequence length ~256. Example using hey:
```
hey -n 20000 -c 800 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" -D payload.json https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
3) Watch `redwood_runtime_queue_length` and `redwood_runtime_batch_backlog` metrics. You should see queue depth climb and tail latency spike; after hitting MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH runtime will start returning 502/504.

sam_sre: I ran a quick burst in a sandbox: confirmed. With MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH=512 and BATCH_WINDOW_MS=10 we see p99 grow to 11-13s and gateway 504s at queue_limit hit. Reproduces reliably when concurrent > ~700 with our current instance count.

aj_oncall: Immediate mitigation for prod? Options:
- throttle inbound traffic via API gateway (rate limit the customer)
- increase MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH temporarily
- reduce BATCH_WINDOW_MS to reduce batching delay and keep tail latency down
- enable fast-path low-latency routing to smaller model variant

jin_runtime: Immediate steps I recommend now (short-lived):
1) Apply per-customer throttle for Acme at the gateway to smooth the burst (we can push a rule in 30s).
2) Simultaneously lower BATCH_WINDOW_MS from 10 -> 5ms on the affected runtime pool to reduce batch formation delay. This reduces throughput slightly but cuts tail latency.
3) If we're still seeing queue_limit tripping, bump MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH 512 -> 1024 for 15 minutes while we monitor.

sam_sre: I'll prepare the Prometheus alert thresholds we should have triggered: queue_depth > 0.75 * MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH for > 2m. Right now our alerting only looks at CPU/memory and request error rate; we missed queue saturation signal.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted: change BATCH_WINDOW_MS=5 on pool prod-model-13b-01 by jin_runtime. Rollout to 25% then 100% if healthy.

jin_runtime: Rolling out the reduced batch window patch to 25% now. Watch latency dashboards.

sam_sre: After the 25% rollout we see a small improvement in p95 and p99; after 100% rollout at 14:33, p99 dropped from ~12s to ~6s, and gateway timeouts decreased significantly. Queue depth still peaked but didn't hit the hard limit after the bump to 1024 (we also applied a short bump).

aj_oncall: What about customer-facing resolution notes? Maria, can you update the support ticket with what we did and ETA for a follow-up?

maria_support: Will do. Drafting message: "We observed request queue saturation on our serving cluster during your traffic spike. We temporarily reduced batch window and increased queue depth which restored service. To prevent recurrence we recommend smoothing bursts (rate limiting) or using a dedicated pool for high-QPS periods. Our infra team will follow up with a permanent fix." Would y'all like me to include any telemetry graphs?

dana_cs: Please include p99 latency graph and the timestamped before/after showing reduced 504s. Add note about optional Dedicated capacity for sustained bursts.

sam_sre: Root cause summary for internal postmortem: sudden customer traffic spike caused continuous-batching backlog -> queue depth hit configured MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH -> runtime fast-fail behavior produced 502/504 gateway responses -> customer saw timeouts. Contributing factors: no alert on high queue depth; default MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH conservative for bursty customers; batch window setting increased tail-latency under burst.

aj_oncall: Action items (assignments):
- sam_sre: create infra alert for queue_depth > 75% of configured limit (P0, 24h).
- jin_runtime: propose safer autoscaling behaviour for batching/backlog and toggle to prefer latency during bursts (P1, 7d).
- product/ops: evaluate default MAX_QUEUE_DEPTH and consider per-tenant defaults or burst-safe profiles (P2, 14d).
- maria_support/dana_cs: follow up with customer and offer credits + docs on burst handling (P1, 48h).

maria_support: Customer updated; they're ok for now and appreciated the quick fix. I'll leave the ticket open until we've completed the follow-ups.

aj_oncall: Thanks everyone. Leaving notes for postmortem. If anything else crops up, re-open this thread.

sam_sre: I'll start the postmortem draft and include the PromQL queries, the staging repro steps, and screenshots of the before/after dashboards.

maria_support: Closing comment — please ping me when postmortem is ready so I can attach it to the support case.

jin_runtime: Also adding a follow-up tweak: consider a dynamic batch window that scales down when queue_depth > 50% to proactively limit tail-latency. I'll prototype in sandbox.

aj_oncall: Noted. Thread closed for now.
